editorial:
Imagine living in a world where you and your sibling are the only two people who truly matter. You get to follow Linus and Vanja, two teens who feel totally disconnected from everyone else, including their mom who is always working night shifts. At first, it just seems like they are very close, but as you watch them over a month, you notice a strange tension. They start to feel like they are the only ones who understand each other, and that bond turns into something much more intense and forbidden. It is a slow-burn story that focuses on the feeling of being lonely and finding comfort in the wrong place.

The acting feels very real, and you can tell the actors put a lot of work into showing guilt and shame without saying too much. While the plot is heavy and might make you feel a bit uncomfortable, it handles the taboo subject in a way that feels honest. If you like dramas that dive deep into complicated family secrets, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find a 4K Blu-ray for your collection, but renting it on Apple TV is a quick and easy way to experience it tonight.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, the siblings can no longer hide their relationship from the world. The guilt and the lies finally catch up to them, leading to a breaking point where their secret is exposed. They realize that their bond has destroyed their ability to live normal lives with other people. The movie ends on a heavy note, showing that while they found love in each other, it came at a cost that they cannot undo.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense character studies and risky dramas.
